claims.text: The POL-RD-01 threshold is met on this trip's own trace: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 17.14 km against a platform optimal of 9.6 km, an excess of 7.54 km — 78.5% of optimal — which passes both the greater-than-20% test and the greater-than-0.8 km test POL-RD-01 requires for an ESTABLISHED deviation. The governing measurement is the trace figure, not trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.1 km, which POL-RD-01 says may NOT be cited for the threshold test.

The excess of 78.5% also exceeds 50% of optimal, so this is a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check must be run. It is run and it does not fire: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 150 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat pattern is established on the trailing-90-day figures and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows from POL-RD-06. I note openly that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and may not be substituted for the 90-day figure under POL-GEN-01. The rider's remedy therefore rests on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic below.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on identity as well as on excess: trip identifier TRP-00509 and the start timestamp 2026-08-28T15:16:40+08:00 are common to the trip_record (started_at), the gps_trace (first_fix_at) and the fare_breakdown's charged trip, so all three admitted artifacts describe the same trip.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 193 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec of 0.0 and no straight-line jump over 500 m, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire. No independent corroboration is required by POL-RD-07(ii) and the mandatory escalation in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

With the excess shown on an unimpaired trace, the burden shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08, and his own account — 'I'm new to the north side and the navigation kept re-routing… I got lost' — points to no exculpatory clause on this record. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log; the chat log for this trip holds zero messages over zero message_count, so no instruction exists to corroborate, no waypoint_hint can even be tested, and the clause is unavailable.

The driver's explanation that navigation kept re-routing and he got lost is an external traffic/navigation excuse, tested under POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00509-01, is IMPAIRED to the point of absence: its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and it carries no payload, so the advisory comparison cannot be run at all. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cited no advisory evidence ID, that absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and the deviation stands at the measured figure against the booked optimal route.

No relocation route under POL-RD-05 is open to the driver: original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. The booked optimal of 9.6 km and 14.0 minutes stands as the baseline for the recomputation.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 (upfront-quoted fares) does not apply and the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs in the ordinary way; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play and the excess is measured against the 9.6 km platform optimal for this solo trip.

Running POL-RD-02 on the fare_breakdown's own figures: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 × 9.6 optimal km + 0.28 × 14.0 optimal min) × the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN, + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting_time_fee − 0 promo_discount = SGD 15.72. Charged_total is SGD 26.39, so the refund is 26.39 − 15.72 = SGD 10.67, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 10.70. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and equals 40.4% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and not FULL_REFUND.

Nothing may be stacked on top of that figure under POL-RD-09: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, airport_surcharge is 0.0, waiting_time_fee is 0.0 and the off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, and the POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends the whole difference between charged_total and the recomputed optimal fare. The arithmetic engages no POL-RD-10 trigger and the case can be decided on this record rather than sent to a human reviewer: the refund of SGD 10.67 is below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), trip identifier TRP-00509 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no artifact timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes, and every charge component of the SGD 26.39 is accounted for by the metered fare lines.

On the rider side of POL-RD-08, rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition the clause attaches to low-value claims does not apply — and it would not bite here in any event, because the excess on this trip is 78.5% of optimal rather than below 30%.

NO_ACTION would not be a neutral outcome here. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are; this is a rider-filed dispute with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so NO_ACTION would leave the rider bearing the entire SGD 26.39 for a trip whose own telemetry records it running 78.5% beyond the platform's optimal route. The evidence supports a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.70 instead.

claims.text: The measure of this dispute is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, not the SGD 26.39 the rider asks for. charged_total is 26.39, and the recomputed fare for the booked 9.6 km / 14.0 min optimal route is 15.72 (base fare 3.80 + distance 7.20 + time 3.92 + platform fee 0.80, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, no ERP and no fixed surcharge), leaving a refund of 10.70 and no more. That is the ceiling on the driver's exposure on this trip.

The rider's consequential losses - the missed bus, the replacement ticket and the lost evening - are not a remedy this policy provides. POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic and traceable to lines of the fare breakdown only, and POL-GEN-03 defines a PARTIAL_REFUND as the return of part of the contested amount, so nothing beyond the 10.70 fare differential can issue however the rider characterises the trip.

The full-fare outcome is not available either: the refund of 10.70 is 40.4% of charged_total, well under the 90% share that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-02, so the base fare, the platform fee and the fare the rider would have paid on the optimal route all stand.

The material deviation does not license a FULL_REFUND uplift or a driver-conduct referral. POL-RD-06's pattern test runs on the trailing-90-day counters and both limbs fail: deviation_flags_90d is 0 (below 3), and 0 flags over 150 completed trips in the window is a ratio of 0.00, below the 0.05 threshold with completed_trips_90d of at least 40. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is likewise 0 but is not the field POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it.

Nothing may be added on top of the recomputed fare. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll line (erp_lines total 0.00, off-optimal-route total 0.00, tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, so POL-RD-09's pass-through corrections are nil on this trip and its anti-double-count rule bars adding any pass-through figure to the 10.70.

The rider's assertion that he was set down at the wrong building buys no adjustment under POL-RD-05. The trip record shows dropoff_amended_at, pickup_amended_at, original_dropoff and amended_optimal_distance_km all null: there is no amended endpoint and no stored amended optimal, so no re-quote can be run and the booked optimal of 9.6 km stands as the only baseline for POL-RD-01.

In the alternative, the record cannot answer the driver's explanation at all, and that gap is a reason to hold the disputed amount rather than refund it. The driver's account is that the navigation kept re-routing him on an unfamiliar corridor - an external cause - and the traffic advisory that POL-RD-03 requires in order to test any such cause is absent: EV-ADVIS-00509-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT at BLOCKING severity, no advisory covering the optimal corridor in this window being on file, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. Invoking POL-RD-03 against an artifact missing from the pool is an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5), and POL-RD-13 expressly does not narrow that route where the party cites the missing identifier; the disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer instead of being refunded on a record that cannot test the explanation.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this trip is a route deviation and the fare for distance and time is reduced accordingly.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. The GPS trace for TRP-00509 (EV-GPS-00509) records 17.14 km driven between the pickup and dropoff events; the platform's optimal route for the booked endpoints is 9.6 km (EV-TRIP-00509). The excess is 7.54 km, or 78.5% of optimal. That passes both POL-RD-01 tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and because it also exceeds 50% it is a MATERIAL deviation. The trace figure governs: POL-RD-01 says the rounded 17.1 km copy on the trip record may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace is also clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 - 193 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds - so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. Your account is that you are new to the north side, the navigation kept re-routing and you got lost. No traffic advisory covers this trip's window: EV-ADVIS-00509-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING). Under POL-RD-13 an external-cause assertion that names no advisory identifier cannot be invoked against one - you named none, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route. The driver-side suggestion that this should instead be held for a human reviewer is rejected for the same reason: no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire.

CHECKS THAT DO NOT CHANGE THE OUTCOME. No relocation is in play - pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, original_pickup, original_dropoff and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 gives the driver no adjustment and 9.6 km stands as the only baseline. The fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is irrelevant. The POL-RD-06 pattern test runs and does not fire: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 150 completed trips in the 90-day window, and 0 divided by 150 is below the 0.05 ratio - so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used for any finding.

THE MONEY. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 9.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 14.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00509) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting-time fee - 0 promo discount = 14.92 + 0.80 = 15.72. charged_total was 26.39. Refund = 26.39 - 15.72 = 10.67, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 10.70. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis and is 40.4% of the charge, below the 90% that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND - so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND. No pass-through figure may be added on top: there are no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, and POL-RD-09 bars double counting the difference the POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends.

THE RIDER'S CONSEQUENTIAL LOSSES. The missed bus, the replacement ticket and the lost evening are not a remedy this policy provides. POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic and traceable to lines of the fare breakdown only, and POL-GEN-03 defines a partial refund as the return of part of the contested amount. That part of your claim cannot be granted, and the SGD 26.39 you ask for is not available; the SGD 10.70 above is the whole of your recovery on this trip.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact that carries a deciding fact - the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown - is admitted at weight 1.0, so the cap on confidence is 1.0.

I got lost') names no advisory evidence ID, so under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one: the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction.
